Hannah / team — ran a quick sizing pass based on Morgan's numbers and the Q3 slice. Short version: two viable configs. Details below. Attachment: capacity_proposal_SKYBRIDGE_v1.xlsx

Option A — 90-day burst top-up (fastest time-to-provision)
- Add: 8 x burst H100 slots (shared burst pool)
- Pros: immediate relief, lower up-front commit, preserves flexibility
- Cons: not SLA-backed at committed latency; potential cold-starts on re-provisioning; price per-hour higher
- Expected 99th pct latency improvement: from ~420ms -> ~220ms on your observed workload

Option B — Convert to committed Dedicated add (preferred for predictability)
- Add: 4 x committed H100 GPUs to Dedicated pool + 4 x burst buffer for seasonal spikes
- Pros: guaranteed throughput under SLA, lower unit cost for sustained usage, predictable tail latency
- Cons: requires 14-21 day provisioning lead time for Dedicated capacity depending on tranche and thermal profiling
- Expected 99th pct latency: ~160ms (steady state) with fallback models kept to same precision

Thermal / slot note: if you convert to committed H100s, data center-side rack/slot constraints could force a staggered onboarding; recommend a runbook that provisions 2 GPUs/week to validate thermal and network saturation. Connor, please confirm the staging cadence and any constraints on your side.

Fallback model guidance (if provisioning delayed):
- Primary: switch to optimized quantized variant (8-bit) of the same model — preserves quality with ~1.2x token throughput increase
- Secondary: reduce max context window and apply aggressive KV cache reuse for stateless short-chat to reduce per-token cost

Ben — quick cost bullets to pass to Hannah for Morgan (ballpark numbers):
- Option A: burst pool estimated $Xk/month (higher per-token)
- Option B: committed 4x H100 estimated $Yk/month (lower per-token, committed discount) + DocuSign SOW for tranche

Karthik
